blurb:
Cody came back to the shelter not because anything was wrong with him, but because his last family just couldn't keep up. He's a three-year-old Cattle Dog mix, about 33 pounds, and the volunteers describe him as a strong and lovable guy with a sweet nature. That tracks. He went through the Prison Pups immersive training program, he loves other dogs, and he actually enjoyed doggie daycare when his previous family took him. He's not a difficult dog. He's just a busy one.

He's got energy, and he's not pretending otherwise. Cattle Dogs are wired to move and think and have a job to do. Give him long walks, a dog park, weekend hikes, or a backyard to run in and he's going to thrive. He calmed right down during his shelter bath when the pets and scratches came, so there's a mellow side in there too. He just needs an outlet first.

He does great with other dogs and liked the kids he met in his previous home. No toddlers though since he's strong and fast and could accidentally knock a small kid over without meaning to. Cats are unknown. He's in the Mostly Mutts training program and has been soaking up everything they've thrown at him.

Mostly Mutts is a rescue based in Kennesaw. You can start the adoption process through their website or stop by to meet Cody in person.
scoring_notes:
• Returned through no fault of his own and completed elite Prison Pups training — a strong redemption angle for readers
• High-energy Cattle Dog with real placement constraints means he's likely been passed over repeatedly despite obvious appeal
• Return-to-shelter status combined with specific household requirements points to a meaningful time investment at Mostly Mutts

blurb:
Cecelia was adopted once already. Nine months in, something changed in her world, and she came back to the shelter shut down and scared. The volunteers say she was a completely different dog from how she'd been before. That says a lot about what she went through. It also says a lot about what she's capable of, because she's come back from it.

She's three years old, about 37 pounds, a Terrier and Boxer mix, and now in a foster home where she's doing great. She already knows sit, stay, come, and leave it. She's in the Mostly Mutts University training program. And her foster family, who actually lives with her, says she is the perfect housemate. When she trusts you, she does full-body wags and tries to climb into your lap despite not being a lap-sized dog.

She does have some history with stranger anxiety, especially with men, and she'll snap as a warning if she feels cornered or grabbed unexpectedly. She's not hiding that and neither are we. What she needs is someone who won't rush her. Let her come to you. Give her a week or two. She'll get there, and when she does, she's going to be all in.

She'd do best as the only dog in the home, and the rescue recommends calmer kids 15 and up. But for the right person with some patience, she's going to be an incredibly loyal companion.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Submit an inquiry on their website to set up a meet.
scoring_notes:
• Returned after nine months and rebuilt from shutdown to thriving — one of the most emotionally compelling arcs in this entire set
• Foster family calls her the perfect housemate; the contrast between her trauma history and her current warmth is a natural editorial centerpiece
• Placement constraints and a second pass through the shelter signal significant wait time, making her feature both timely and urgent

blurb:
Eight years old, 58 pounds, rescued from animal control, and her foster mom says adopters will hit the jackpot with her. That's not shelter marketing talk. That's someone who actually lives with this dog.

Yasmeen is a Lab and Terrier mix who went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and came out the other side knowing how to be a great companion. She's warm, she's loyal, and she does well with other dogs once she gets past her initial this-is-my-person moment. She was fine with the boxer she stayed with during foster coverage, and she's good with cats too. She just likes to know she can trust you first. Once she does, you've got a devoted dog who wants to be close to her people.

She does have some guarding instincts around strangers coming into the home, and the rescue recommends a household with dog-savvy kids 15 and up because of that. It's not aggression, it's protectiveness, and she's actively worked on it in training. If you want to bring kids younger than that to meet her, they can set that up with her trainer.

Senior dogs get overlooked constantly, and Yasmeen has already put in the work. She's trained, she's in a foster home right now, and she just needs someone to take her the rest of the way.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Visit their site to start an adoption inquiry.
scoring_notes:
• Senior dogs are statistically the least adopted demographic — her story is the highest-urgency feature opportunity in this batch
• Foster mom's unprompted "jackpot" endorsement is a powerful, credible testimonial that translates directly to newsletter copy
• Prison Pups graduate, cat-compatible, and foster-placed yet still waiting — the gap between her qualifications and her adoption status is the story

blurb:
Loafer is a tiny tuxedo kitten with a very specific policy about meeting new people: he's going to watch you from across the room first, figure out if you're worth his time, and then slowly, on his own schedule, decide you're actually pretty great. His foster mom describes him and his siblings as "a great group of kittens," and Loafer is the curious one. He wants to know everything that's going on. He just wants to learn about it from a safe spot.

Once he warms up, you get a playful, adventurous little guy who loves chasing toys, wrestling with his siblings, and climbing anything he can get his paws on. His foster home also has a ferret, which Loafer apparently takes completely in stride. So if your house is a little chaotic, he's probably going to fit right in.

He does best with gentle kids who won't rush him, and he'd likely love having another cat around. He's litter trained, microchipped, and up to date on his shots. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can visit in person or check out his profile at mostlymutts.org to get the process started. Adoption fee is $175.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Playful, curious tuxedo kitten with broad household compatibility including chaos, kids, and other pets
• Relatable "slow-to-warm" personality gives readers an endearing hook without red flags
• Recent foster placement suggests a short wait; lower urgency than longer-term candidates

blurb:
Cannoli came into Mostly Mutts straight from animal control, barely two pounds and not yet 10 weeks old. He's a little tuxedo kitten who's still getting his bearings, still figuring out that people are actually on his side. The volunteers have been putting in the time with him, and it's working. He's already starting to enjoy the petting and the attention coming his way.

He gets along well with his siblings, so he'd likely do great in a home that already has a cat. If you've got a gentle cat at home who'd appreciate a small, playful buddy, Cannoli might be the right fit. He's litter trained, up to date on kitten vaccines, microchipped, and already neutered.

He's a little shy right now, but that's just where he is in the process. Give him time and a patient household and he'll come around fast. He's at the shelter in Kennesaw. Adoption fee is $175. Visit mostlymutts.org or stop by to meet him in person.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Animal control rescue narrative paired with active volunteer rehabilitation creates a feel-good progress story
• Already neutered and fully vetted at under 10 weeks — unusually adoption-ready for a shy kitten
• Shyness and shelter origin suggest a moderate wait, but no indicators of an especially long stay

blurb:
Benedict started his life in someone's garage, born to a feral mom who wasn't sticking around. A good neighbor stepped in and got the litter to Mostly Mutts. Most of his siblings have already been adopted. Benedict is still waiting for his turn.

He's about 2.5 months old, a fluffy medium-haired kitten with a social, affectionate personality that you don't always see at that age. He chases toys, pounces on shadows, and explores everything within reach. Then he finds someone to curl up on and purrs until you can't remember what you were doing before he showed up. Litter trained, microchipped, and already socialized well with other kittens.

He still needs to finish his kitten vaccination series and will need to be neutered once he's big enough, so there's a little follow-through involved. But honestly, that's true of any kitten. Benedict is living in the Kitty Room at the Mostly Mutts shelter in Kennesaw. Stop by and meet him, or visit mostlymutts.org to learn more. Adoption fee is $175.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Feral-born survivor with a naturally social personality is a rare and compelling combination for readers
• Still waiting while his siblings have all been adopted — a built-in emotional urgency that resonates in print
• Currently shelter-housed rather than fostered, signaling a longer or less certain path to adoption
